Security & Privacy First

Your connections travel. Keys stay on-device.

The sync server only receives auth proofs and an AES-256-GCM encrypted vault. Account keys are derived client-side with scrypt. Self-host the server or work offline without signing in.

Understand synchronization →

What gets synced

  • ✓ Connections and workspaces in an AES-256-GCM vault.
  • ✓ Database contents and SSH/SSL files are not synced.
  • ✓ Signing out keeps your local data.

Password recovery is not available. A forgotten password cannot decrypt the server vault; read the limitations before enabling sync.

Self-Host Infrastructure

Deploy your private sync server in minutes.

Choose localhost for local evaluation, or HTTPS with Caddy for multiple devices. Docker Compose configuration is generated in your browser.

Deployment settings

Start and check

Terminal
docker compose up -d

Save the files in one directory, run the command and open the URL above. Append /healthz to check the server. Inspect status with docker compose ps and logs with docker compose logs --tail=100. Retain the sqlpro-data volume when upgrading.

FAQ

Clear answers to common questions.

Learn more about features, security, compatibility, and troubleshooting in the documentation.

Troubleshooting and support →
Do I need an account?

No. Database connections, the SQL editor, backups and import/export work 100% offline. An account is only needed for sync across devices.

Does it support PostgreSQL or SQL Server?

Currently SqlPro focuses deeply on MySQL and MariaDB. Other connection types are safely skipped during Navicat import.

What if I forget my sync password?

To ensure true Zero-Knowledge security, no recovery keys are stored on the server. If forgotten, server vault cannot be decrypted, but your local machine data remains completely intact.

Are SSH private keys synced?

Only file paths are synced. Private keys and certificates always stay local on each device and are never sent over the network.

Which installer should I choose?

Windows: choose the standard installer (.exe) or Portable version. Ubuntu/Linux: use .deb package or AppImage. Installers are optimized for x64 architecture.
